name: Cóiced

attributes.attribute: the fifth province and a cosmological idea
a province formed near the middle of Ireland

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cóiced is an Irish mythic theme tied to the provinces of the island. The word means a fifth. Four of those provinces were purely geographic. Leinster lay in the east. Munster stood in the southwest. Connacht covered the west. Ulster rose in the north. The fifth province, Mide, or Meath, was not so much a land as a cosmological idea. It stood for the true center of the country. People sometimes placed that center on the hill of Uisneach. Others pointed to a rock on that hill called the Stone of Divisions. In historical times a province of Meath was set up near the middle of Ireland. The mystical air of the old divisions never faded.

okr.objective: Cóiced names the five provinces of ancient Ireland.
key_results: The term Cóiced means a fifth.
Leinster, Munster, Connacht, and Ulster were the four geographic provinces.
Mide or Meath was the fifth province as a cosmological idea.
Its center was the hill of Uisneach with the Stone of Divisions.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
